If you're interested, the system is The End of the World series by Fantasy Flight Games. It was fun, but like you said, it's a pretty easy scenario to run in any system and the books aren't (in my opinion) worth the price. I think they're planning on 4 general scenarios- zombies, gods, machines, and aliens.

Due to the nature of our career paths, we started upping the difficulty of scenarios to keep the "Zombie Apocalypse" feel, but with scenarios less in the fantasy fiction realm and more grounded in reality. Although, sometimes we still throw those in as the occasional curve. We do power grid failures, food shortages/crop plagues, natural disasters, various CBR scenarios, foreign invasions and martial law, often a combination of the aforementioned, generally on a global scale. Again... career paths. You'd be surprised, or maybe not, how many bases & camps in Iraq, Afghanistan, and parts of Africa have contingency plans & SOPs for those scenarios now.

Rules-wise, we've experimented with various systems and now use an in-house modified hybrid of the old West End Games Star Wars d6 system and White Wolf with rolls on modified success difficulties. We incorporate a wild die to allow for unintended and often unforeseeable consequences even in successful attempts, or failed, for that matter. All equipment statistics are generated based on actual real-world characteristics then converted to SI measures to make it easier to work in a primarily d10 system.

Being in shape is awesome, don't get me wrong, but it never hurts to have the mind and imagination to back it up when the needs arise. And hell, a good portion of what I've done is nothing more than weaponized math anyway.
